symptoms: Connection timeouts between Checkout API and downstream cache

historical_incidents.title: Checkout service latency after cache configuration deployment
symptoms: Redis evictions after a configuration release
historical_incidents.confirmed_root_cause: Redis max-memory policy and connection-pool configuration caused cache churn and downstream saturation
historical_incidents.failed_mitigation: restarting Checkout API pods did not resolve the issue.

historical_incidents.title: Payment authorization delays caused by queue-consumer saturation
historical_incidents.confirmed_root_cause: Consumer thread pool contention during high throughput authorization batch
successful_resolution: partition queue traffic across secondary topic
historical_incidents.failed_mitigation: purging pending message dead-letter queue caused data inconsistency.

historical_incidents.title: Azure SQL connection exhaustion caused by a pool leak and aggressive retry policy
historical_incidents.confirmed_root_cause: Unclosed connections in unhandled checkout exception path combined with exponential retry storms
successful_resolution: apply connection pool clamp and circuit breaker
historical_incidents.failed_mitigation: increasing max pool size to 500 overwhelmed the database CPU.
historical_incidents.runbook_used: Azure SQL Connection Pool Exhaustion Procedure

fix_outcomes.action_description: Revert Redis connection pool parameters and max-memory policy to v4.18.1 baseline.

fix_outcomes.action_title: Restart Checkout API pods (INEFFECTIVE - FAILED MITIGATION)
fix_outcomes.action_description: Rolling restart of Checkout API deployment pods across Kubernetes cluster.
fix_outcomes.verification_metric: Did not resolve eviction or pool exhaustion; introduced additional cold-start latency.
fix_outcomes.hazard_warning: CRITICAL HAZARD: Restarting pods under Redis eviction storms causes instant cold cache stampedes and exacerbates p95 latency.

fix_outcomes.action_description: Scale Redis instance tier from P2 to P3 to provide headroom during configuration rollback.

fix_outcomes.action_title: Validate eviction rate & gradually restore normal traffic limits
fix_outcomes.action_description: Confirm Redis key eviction metrics stabilize at 0 ops/sec before removing temporary throttle.
fix_outcomes.verification_metric: p95 latency returns under 250ms and error rate < 0.1%

fix_outcomes.action_description: Increase HPA minimum replicas for Kafka queue worker service.

fix_outcomes.action_title: Apply connection pool clamp & circuit breaker
fix_outcomes.action_description: Throttle client connection attempts to Azure SQL to prevent pool thrashing.
fix_outcomes.runbook_title: Azure SQL Connection Pool Exhaustion Procedure

team_knowledge.escalation_policy: P1 alerts require on-call engagement within 5 minutes. Bridge channel #incident-checkout-p1.
operational_constraints: All cache configuration changes must go through 5% canary deployment.
Pod restarts during active eviction storms are prohibited due to stampede risk.
Production changes during peak retail windows (12:00-18:00 UTC) require SRE lead signoff.

runbooks.title: Redis Latency and Eviction Response
runbooks.author: Azure Platform Architecture
runbooks.summary: Standard operating procedure for responding to Redis max-memory eviction cascades and connection pool saturation.

steps.name: Verify Eviction Rate
steps.intent: Confirm whether memory limit policy (allkeys-lru / volatile-lru) is evicting active session keys.

steps.name: Roll Back Recent Cache Config Release
steps.intent: Immediately revert any newly applied connection-pool or max-memory limits to known good baseline.

steps.name: Temporarily Scale Cache Capacity
steps.intent: Provide burst buffer memory while cache rewarms.

steps.name: Validate Latency Stabilization
steps.intent: Ensure p95 latency falls below 250ms before releasing incident response bridge.
